biography: Marzio Romano, born in the shadow of the Imola circuit, practically inhaled gasoline fumes from infancy. His father, a mechanic for a local touring car team, instilled a love for motorsport early on, smuggling young Marzio into the paddock to watch legends like Michael Schumacher and Fernando Alonso. Romano began karting at age 8, displaying a raw, untamed talent that quickly caught the eye of talent scouts. His aggressive style led to numerous victories, but also frequent crashes, earning him a reputation as a 'wild card'. After dominating the Italian Formula 3 series, he made the jump to GT racing, landing a coveted seat with Lamborghini. While initial seasons were marred by inconsistency and over-aggression, Romano has matured into a formidable competitor, consistently challenging for podiums and establishing himself as a key figure within the team. He's currently in his fifth season with Lamborghini, eyeing the GT World Challenge title.
drivingStyle: Romano's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos'. He's an incredibly late-braker, often diving into corners with a ferocity that leaves rivals scrambling. While this aggressive approach can sometimes lead to mistakes, it also allows him to execute daring overtakes and extract maximum performance from the car. He's known for his exceptional car control, particularly in wet conditions, and his ability to manage tire degradation under immense pressure – often pushing them to the very limit.
